newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore urged to shed authoritarian style of rule.
newsitem.headline: Singapore urged to shed authoritarian style of rule.

text.p: Opposition leader Chee Soon Juan on Wednesday urged Singaporeans to shed what he called an authoritarian style of government dominated by the long-ruling People's Action Party (PAP).
"I'd really like to be able to see our society open up," Chee, secretary-general of the Social Democratic Party (SDP), told the Foreign Correspondents' Association of Singapore.

"I see this continued authoritarian style of government really not going to be of any good to our society, be it economically, politically or socially. People in Singapore, we behave more out of fear than we do out of hope," he said.

The PAP, which has governed Singapore for more than 30 years, makes no apologies for a style of rule that has taken the small nation past Britain, its former colonial ruler, in terms of per capita income.
But Chee said a PAP government would not be able to guarantee continued prosperity if it stifled people's creativity.
The PAP holds 77 of the 81 elected seats in parliament and is expected to win in general elections due by April next year.
Chee said the SDP, which has three seats, may be able to field up to 15 candidates in the elections.
"If...half of them are successful, that's a major breakthrough," he said.
Chee said the SDP would campaign on the issues of health, transportation and housing costs in Singapore despite a blunder on its handling of a debate on health costs.

In August, the SDP asserted that the government share of total health costs had slid to five percent. Under an onslaught of government denials, it admitted the figure should have been 25 percent and said it made the mistake due to a typographical error.
Health Minister George Yeo formally charged Chee and three other SDP leaders of presenting fabricated evidence to the parliamentary panel conducting hearings on the issue.
If Chee and his colleagues are found guilty, they could be fined up to Singapore $50,000 (US$35,460) or jailed for the entire current session of parliament.
Chee avoided detailed comment on the charges.
He said the SDP faced a tough election campaign in which it could expect no help from the government-linked Singapore media.
"(An) independent press is something Singapore needs," he said. "We're always at the mercy of the local media."
The PAP, led by now Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew, has led the flourishing city-state since independence in 1965.
